archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (backed-in division winner)
archetype.definition: Houston outlasted a weak AL West at 81-81 despite being outscored by 32 runs, then lost both Wild Card games at home to Chicago.

report.headline: Outscored, carried by close games, crowned in a weak West, gone in two

recap.finish: 81-81, won the AL West by one game; lost the Wild Card Series 0-2 to CHW
recap.body:
This was a .500 team that the standings flattered. Houston scored 734 runs and allowed 766, a Run Diff / G of -0.2 that ranked 19th of 30. It still won the AL West because the division gave it room: Texas finished one game back at 80-82 and nobody else got close. The W vs Run Diff of +3.2 accounts for the gap between a roughly 78-win run differential and the actual 81. The site's 20th-of-30 ranking is the more honest read of the roster.

The season nearly ended in April. After a 4-2 start, the Astros went 8-18 and were outscored 166-129 that month, which left them 12-20. From May on they were a different, if modest, team: 69-61 over the last five months with run totals almost even. June was the high point at 16-11. September slipped to 11-13, and the division was settled on the final weekend, when they won three of four at the Athletics, including 13-2 and 9-0 routs. That followed a three-game home sweep by Atlanta that had made the finish tense.

The lineup was Yordan Alvarez and not much else. His 181 wRC+, 42 homers and 6.8 WAR made him the top DH on the site. Isaac Paredes (130 wRC+, 4.4 WAR) and Jeremy Peña (124 wRC+ in 112 games) were genuinely good. The rest of the regulars were not. Christian Walker hit 29 homers with a .299 OBP. Jose Altuve had a 97 wRC+ with -8.5 Def Runs at second. The outfield of Cam Smith, Daulton Varsho and Taylor Trammell posted wRC+ marks of 86, 78 and 78. That is how a team OPS that ranked 7th produced only the 13th-best scoring offense and a D grade for the hitters.

Run prevention was the bigger problem and the bigger change. The staff ERA of 4.45 and the Def Rank both sat 24th, and the fielders cost 14.8 runs. A year earlier they had saved 27, so that is a swing of more than 40 runs on defense alone. Peter Lambert (3.82 ERA over 155.2 innings) and Hunter Brown (3.19) held up the top of the rotation. Brown managed only 20 starts and walked 12.2% of batters. Behind them, Mike Burrows (5.99, now on the 60-day IL), Tatsuya Imai (4.93 with a 15.1% walk rate) and Cristian Javier (5.14) dragged the group to a C-. The bullpen's B- leaned on Steven Okert's 2.13 ERA and 21 holds. Closer-type Bryan Abreu was erratic, with a 15.3% walk rate and a 4.62 FIP.

The Wild Card Series looked like the regular season. The Astros hosted and lost 6-3 and 7-3. Brown recorded two outs in his start, and Alvarez went 1-for-8. Peña, Smith and Altuve each homered, but the lineup managed a .583 OPS across the two games, and the -3.5 run differential per game ranked 10th of 12 playoff teams.

highlights.title: Alvarez remained an elite bat
highlights.body: Alvarez led the site's DHs with a .316/.432/.601 line and 6.8 WAR, by himself a large share of the team's offensive value. His production is consistent with an established elite hitter rather than a fluke. He is the one fixed point the offense can build around.

highlights.title: Recovery after the April collapse
highlights.body: After a 12-20 start, Houston went 69-61 the rest of the way with roughly even run totals. That was enough to edge Texas by one game. It shows the roster was a .500-ish team rather than an April-level disaster, but not much better than that.

highlights.title: Infield core and Okert
highlights.body: Paredes (4.4 WAR, 130 wRC+) and Peña (3.4 WAR in 112 games) gave the lineup two above-average regulars. Okert's 2.13 ERA and 21 holds anchored a bullpen that graded B-. His 3.23 FIP suggests some regression from that ERA but a genuinely solid reliever.

lowlights.title: Run prevention collapsed with the defense
lowlights.body: The 4.45 ERA ranked 24th, and Fielding Runs went from +27 in 2025 to -14.8. That reverses one of the franchise's longtime strengths. Altuve's -8.5 Def Runs at second and Peña's -4.8 at short point to an infield that no longer converts outs.

lowlights.title: Back of the rotation
lowlights.body: Burrows, Imai and Javier combined for about 234 innings with ERAs between 4.93 and 5.99. Imai's 15.1% walk rate undercut his strikeout stuff. With Brown limited to 20 starts, too many innings went to pitchers who couldn't hold games.

lowlights.title: A record propped up by luck
lowlights.body: An outscored team finishing .500 owed about three wins to close games. This is the second straight year the W vs Run Diff ran positive (+3.7 in 2025). That kind of edge rarely persists, so the underlying team is closer to a 78-win club.

arc.note: An 8-18 April sank them to 12-20 before a steady 69-61 climb over the last five months. They clinched the West in a final-weekend split at the Athletics, then went out in two home playoff games.

recap.nextYear: The five-year trend is the real story. Run Diff / G has fallen every season, from 1.35 in 2022 to 0.13 in 2025 to -0.2 now, and this year the defense and pitching gave way after the offense had slipped the year before. The offense ranked 13th in scoring, better than 2025's 21st, but it rests on Alvarez, Paredes and Peña. The outfield and first base produced sub-.300 OBPs that earned the hitters a D grade. Lambert and a healthy Brown are a reasonable top two, and Okert a dependable setup man. Beyond them the rotation needs innings that don't come with a 5-plus ERA, and the infield defense needs fixing. The division title came by one game with three wins of close-game luck. Without real improvement in run prevention, that margin won't repeat.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; postseason is just two games.
